transcript.content: Hi, welcome in, I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I just have this constant feeling like I’ve got a motor humming under my skin whenever I’m supposed to sit still. 

It happens a lot in situations where I have to stay put, like during staff meetings at work, or when I'm sitting through briefings for church events. I just can't seem to stay in my seat. I always end up shifting around, standing up, or just finding some excuse to get up and move around.
Have you felt this restless, need-to-move feeling since you were a child, or is this something that started more recently in your life?

Oh, no, it's... it's definitely been around since I was a kid. I remember getting in trouble a lot back in grade school for popping out of my seat. I'd be talking over the teacher, or just rushing ahead on things before she even finished giving the directions. My mother used to say I acted like I was wound too tight, even back then. So, yeah, it's not a recent thing at all.
Do you also struggle with staying focused on tasks, following through on details, or often losing track of things and getting distracted, even when you're not feeling restless?

No, not really. I mean, I don't have much trouble focusing on what I need to do. When I'm cleaning the building or fixing something up at work, I just get it done. I keep track of my supplies fine, and I don't usually lose things. It's really just the sitting still and the feeling like I need to be moving that bothers me.
Does this restless, need-to-move feeling and impulsiveness show up in other parts of your life too—like at home, in social situations, or when you're relaxing—not just at work or church meetings?

Yeah, it definitely shows up in other places. Even when I’m just trying to relax, it's there. Like, if I go fishing with my wife, or we're sitting through a game of bingo, I can't just... be still. I'll catch myself tapping my foot, or I start talking too loud, or I'm constantly messing with my tackle box or my bingo pencil. It just makes it really hard for me to sit quietly and actually enjoy the downtime.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports lifelong (since grade school) pervasive hyperactivity and impulsivity—restlessness, difficulty remaining seated, excessive movement, talking over others, impulsive actions—present across multiple settings (work, church, home, leisure activities). Inattentive symptoms (task focus, organization, losing items) are explicitly denied, indicating a predominantly hyperactive-impulsive presentation rather than combined or inattentive type. Symptoms began in childhood and have persisted into adulthood, causing functional interference in occupational and social/leisure contexts, consistent with ADHD (Hyperkinetic Disorder), predominantly hyperactive-impulsive presentation.
